attempts.label: CRCNS:mt-3
attempts.entry_title: Perisaccadic responses of MT neurons (Niknam et al. 2019)
attempts.summary: Saccadic suppression in MT held up in this data, with the paper's count of suppressed neurons, but far fewer neurons showed remapping of responses to the future field and the saccade target (11 against the paper's 37 for the saccade target). The Methods do not say what the signed-rank test pairs, and that choice decides the remapping counts; a pairing the Methods exclude comes close to the paper's. The time-varying encoding models, the paper's main contribution, could not be tested: fitting them was far beyond this run's compute limits, and the comparison N-model is described only in an earlier paper. The minor claims on neuron counts and response latency held, and most example neurons matched.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Niknam, Akbarian, Clark, Zamani, Noudoost and Nategh (2019) on CRCNS mt-3, which holds the spike trains, probe sequences and saccade times of 41 MT neurons from 11 sessions. It links the neurons to the RF, FF and ST probes listed in the paper's code, and tests the recorded saccadic suppression, FF- and ST-remapping of Figure 1. The model claims (S-, F-, A- and N-models, Figures 3 to 8) are blocked, with the cost of the S-model timed.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Niknam et al. (2019) from CRCNS mt-3

outcomes.statement: The RF, FF and ST probe of each neuron listed in the code repository's main_lists.mat correspond to the dataset's neurons, and the RF probe recomputed from the dataset by the Methods' definition matches the listed one.
outcomes.source: Methods, Receptive field, future field, and saccade target location estimation; code lib/models/fmodel.m (get_centers) at commit 1438dde
outcomes.notes: All 41 files match a probe_list row by session and channel, and all 41 rows have a file. The RF recomputed by D1 with onsets is the listed RF for 38 neurons and a neighbour for the other 3 (41 of 41; also 41 with every-ms presentations). FF minus RF offsets are (-3, 0) for 26 neurons, (-2, 0) for 1 and (2, 0) for 14, giving 27 leftward and 14 rightward neurons. The neuron files in the code repository are identical to the CRCNS files in all four variables.

outcomes.statement: Of 49 well-isolated MT neurons, 41 responded to the probes and were analysed; they come from 11 sessions, 27 neurons from 9 sessions with leftward saccades and 14 from 2 sessions with rightward saccades.
outcomes.source: Methods, Experimental paradigm and data acquisition, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: In total, data were recorded from 41 MT neurons during 11 recording sessions. In 9 recording sessions, the saccades were made to the left (27 of 41 neurons), and in 2 recording sessions, the saccades were made to the right (14 of 41 neurons).
outcomes.notes: 41 neurons in 11 sessions (first 8 digits of the file name); by the sign of the listed FF minus RF offset, 27 neurons from 9 sessions are leftward and 14 from 2 sessions (20151214, 20151215) rightward, and each session has one direction. Per-session counts match the data descriptor. The 49 isolated units cannot be checked; the 8 discarded are not in the data set, as the descriptor says.
deviations: Saccade direction is not in the data set; it is read from the code's probe_list, as the criterion says.

outcomes.statement: Eight neurons show significant saccadic suppression; for them the average normalized response to an RF probe drops from 2.53 to 1.51 when the probe appears just before the saccade.
outcomes.source: Results, Saccades modulate the responses of MT neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 1B
outcomes.quote: For the subpopulation of neurons with significant saccadic suppression (see Methods ), the average normalized response dropped from 2.53 ± 0.37 to 1.51 ± 0.29 (mean ± SE).
outcomes.notes: Under O1 b with onsets, 8 neurons are significant, and their normalized RF response over 50-75 ms falls from 2.235 +- 0.291 to 1.239 +- 0.183 (O4 a), both within tolerance near its lower edge; the O4 b peaks are 2.541 and 1.530. Reading O1 a cannot be tested. The 8 neurons come from 5 sessions, with p 0.0002 to 0.043. They are only partly the paper's: the code's undocumented nuron_list also marks 8 suppressed neurons, and 5 of them are among these 8 (35 of 41 neurons agree). Variants: unpaired with onsets 9 neurons (2.291 to 1.297); signed-rank over time bins of mean counts 13 and of smoothed curves 15; with every-ms presentations 4 to 16 neurons.
deviations: Pairing by trial (O1 a) cannot be tested: no trial in any session shows the same probe in both the fixation and the perisaccadic window, as a probe returns only after a pass through the whole order (median 562 to 604 ms between repeats per session). The outcome rests on pairing by condition (O1 b), the other reading the criterion lets decide.

Presentations are the first ms of each run of a probe code (O2 i); runs of 14 or 21 ms count once, as such a run takes one place in the probe order (session 20150717, data check). Windows are taken inclusive at 1 ms, as get_mean_resp.m indexes t:t+window, a standard choice. Saccade onset is sample tsaccade in MATLAB's 1-based indexing, as select_bases.m reads it (tsaccade(i) + times).

outcomes.statement: Twenty-three neurons show significant FF-remapping; for them the average normalized response to an FF probe rises from 0.90 during fixation to 1.30 just before the saccade.
outcomes.source: Results, Saccades modulate the responses of MT neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 1C
outcomes.quote: For the subpopulation of neurons with significant FF-remapping, the average normalized response to FF stimuli increased from 0.90 ± 0.03 to 1.30 ± 0.08 (mean ± SE).
outcomes.notes: Under O1 b with onsets 8 neurons show FF-remapping (paper 23), with the normalized late FF response rising from 0.792 +- 0.037 to 1.609 +- 0.111 (paper 0.90 to 1.30); the rise is there but none of the three numbers is within tolerance, so the partial rule (direction and one number) is not met. Reading O1 a cannot be tested. No variant reaches the count (9 to 19 neurons). The closest, the signed-rank test over time bins of the smoothed curves with onsets (19 neurons, 0.885 to 1.411) and the unpaired and time-bin tests with every-ms presentations (17 neurons, 0.888 or 0.889 to 1.427 or 1.430), have only the fixation value within tolerance; they are outside O1 or O2 i and do not decide. The code's nuron_list marks 23 FF neurons; 26 of 41 neurons agree with it under O1 b. Whether O1 should hold a pairing over time bins is asked of a reader (questions/niknam-2019.yaml).
deviations: Pairing by trial (O1 a) cannot be tested: no trial in any session shows the same probe in both the fixation and the perisaccadic window, as a probe returns only after a pass through the whole order (median 562 to 604 ms between repeats per session). The outcome rests on pairing by condition (O1 b), the other reading the criterion lets decide.

Saccade onset is sample tsaccade in MATLAB's 1-based indexing, as select_bases.m reads it (tsaccade(i) + times).

outcomes.statement: Thirty-seven neurons show significant ST-remapping; for them the average normalized late response to a probe near the saccade target rises from 0.83 during fixation to 1.35 just before the saccade.
outcomes.source: Results, Saccades modulate the responses of MT neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 1D
outcomes.quote: For the subpopulation of neurons with significant ST-remapping, the average normalized ST response increased from 0.83 ± 0.03 to 1.35 ± 0.06 (mean ± SE).
outcomes.notes: Under O1 b with onsets 11 neurons show ST-remapping (paper 37), rising from 0.749 +- 0.046 to 1.629 +- 0.112 (paper 0.83 to 1.35); no number within tolerance. Reading O1 a cannot be tested. The outcome depends on the pairing: a signed-rank test over the 1 ms bins of the smoothed response curves gives 34 neurons, 0.815 to 1.365, all three numbers within tolerance, and agrees with the code's nuron_list on ST for 36 of 41 neurons (15 under O1 b). The Methods exclude that test (statistics on spike counts, "not estimates of firing rate") and the claims file does not list it, so it does not decide; whether O1 should hold a pairing over time bins is asked of a reader (questions/niknam-2019.yaml). On mean counts per bin the time-bin test gives 16 neurons with onsets and 29 with every-ms presentations (0.819 to 1.383); the unpaired test with every-ms presentations gives 31 (0.823 to 1.369). The ST probe is taken from probe_list, whose selection used the same perisaccadic increase.
deviations: Pairing by trial (O1 a) cannot be tested: no trial in any session shows the same probe in both the fixation and the perisaccadic window, as a probe returns only after a pass through the whole order (median 562 to 604 ms between repeats per session). The outcome rests on pairing by condition (O1 b), the other reading the criterion lets decide.

outcomes.statement: Twenty-two neurons show both FF- and ST-remapping; for them the normalized FF response rises from 0.90 to 1.32 and the normalized ST response from 0.80 to 1.46.
outcomes.source: Results, Saccades modulate the responses of MT neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 1E
outcomes.quote: For the subpopulation of neurons with significant FF- and ST-remapping, the average normalized FF response increased from 0.90 ± 0.03 to 1.32 ± 0.08 (mean ± SE), and the average normalized ST response increased from 0.80 ± 0.03 to 1.46 ± 0.08 (mean ± SE).
outcomes.notes: Under O1 b with onsets 6 neurons show both effects (paper 22); FF 0.777 to 1.680 and ST 0.750 to 1.789, both rising, none of the five numbers within tolerance (the partial rule needs two). Reading O1 a cannot be tested. The variants give 6 to 19 neurons; the smoothed time-bin test with onsets (19 neurons) and the unpaired, time-bin and smoothed time-bin tests with every-ms presentations (17 neurons) have 3 of 5 numbers within tolerance, the others none. The code's nuron_list has 22 neurons with both. Asked of a reader with fig1d-st-remapping.
deviations: Pairing by trial (O1 a) cannot be tested: no trial in any session shows the same probe in both the fixation and the perisaccadic window, as a probe returns only after a pass through the whole order (median 562 to 604 ms between repeats per session). The outcome rests on pairing by condition (O1 b), the other reading the criterion lets decide.

Windows are taken inclusive at 1 ms, as get_mean_resp.m indexes t:t+window, a standard choice. outcomes.statement: Perisaccadic FF and ST responses come at a longer latency (80-150 ms after the probe) than RF responses (50-75 ms).
outcomes.source: Results, Saccades modulate the responses of MT neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 1C and 1D
outcomes.quote: Note that the perisaccadic FF response occurs at longer latency than RF responses (neurons responding 50–75 ms after stimulus onset for the RF, vs. 80–150 ms after stimulus onset for the FF).
outcomes.notes: The smoothed (FWHM 13 ms) neuron-averaged fixation RF response of all 41 neurons peaks at 62 ms; the perisaccadic FF response of the FF-remapping neurons peaks at 108 ms and the ST response of the ST-remapping neurons at 99 ms under O1 b with onsets. Every testable reading gives RF 59-62 ms, FF 103-108 ms and ST 96-128 ms. The remapped peaks are not an independent test: the neurons are selected for an increase 80-150 ms after onset, which pulls the averaged peak into that window, and single-neuron peaks are spread (FF 12 to 150 ms, ST 0 to 150 ms). The RF peak, over all 41 neurons with no selection, is the part that does not depend on the selection. The selected populations are smaller than the paper's (8 and 11 neurons).
deviations: Pairing by trial (O1 a) cannot be tested: no trial in any session shows the same probe in both the fixation and the perisaccadic window, as a probe returns only after a pass through the whole order (median 562 to 604 ms between repeats per session). The outcome rests on pairing by condition (O1 b), the other reading the criterion lets decide.

Presentations are the first ms of each run of a probe code (O2 i); runs of 14 or 21 ms count once, as such a run takes one place in the probe order (session 20150717, data check). Windows are taken inclusive at 1 ms, as get_mean_resp.m indexes t:t+window, a standard choice. Saccade onset is sample tsaccade in MATLAB's 1-based indexing, as select_bases.m reads it (tsaccade(i) + times).
The measure (peak latency of the smoothed population response) is the criterion's; the paper states the latencies from its figure.

outcomes.statement: In example neurons the RF response falls from 60.89 to 40.49 spk/s before the saccade; the late FF response rises from 7.90 to 18.42 spk/s; the late ST response rises from 23.80 to 64.64 spk/s; and in a neuron with both effects FF rises from 15.83 to 39.10 and ST from 16.15 to 36.17 spk/s, each with p < 0.001.
outcomes.source: Results, Saccades modulate the responses of MT neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 1B to 1E, left panels
outcomes.quote: For the example neuron, the average response to an RF stimulus dropped from 60.89 ± 2.82 (mean ± SE) spk/s during fixation to 40.49 ± 12.64 (mean ± SE) spk/s when the stimulus appeared just prior to saccade onset (example neuron, p < 0.001).

statistics.about: each of the five example-neuron comparisons
statistics.test: Wilcoxon one-sided signed-rank test (Methods, Statistical analysis of perisaccadic responses)

outcomes.notes: With onsets, three of four examples are matched on both values and a significant D2 test under O1 b: FF example 2015071702 (7.83 to 18.96 spk/s, p 0.017), ST example 2015092707 (23.61 to 64.64, p 0.0059), example with both 2015051115 (FF 15.76 to 39.10, p 0.00063; ST 16.05 to 36.17, p 0.00037). Perisaccadic means equal the paper's to the second decimal for 64.64, 39.10 and 36.17, so these are likely the paper's neurons. No neuron matches the RF example; 2015092709 has the paper's perisaccadic 40.49 +- 12.64 but a fixation rate of 56.94 +- 2.71 against 60.89 +- 2.82, and p 0.49 under O1 b (0.02 unpaired); fixation windows starting -560 to -440 ms and ending -160 to -40 ms give it 53.87 to 59.68, never 60.89. With every-ms presentations (variant) 2015083106 matches the RF example. The paper's p < 0.001 holds under O1 b only for the example with both effects; the unpaired test gives p 0.00011 or less for all three matched examples. Their fixation rates differ from the paper's by 0.07 to 0.19 spk/s with SEs equal within 0.01, and no single fixation window in the scan matches all three (closest -495 to -100 ms, within 0.054 spk/s); the paper's fixation set is not identified.
deviations: Pairing by trial (O1 a) cannot be tested: no trial in any session shows the same probe in both the fixation and the perisaccadic window, as a probe returns only after a pass through the whole order (median 562 to 604 ms between repeats per session). The outcome rests on pairing by condition (O1 b), the other reading the criterion lets decide.

Presentations are the first ms of each run of a probe code (O2 i); runs of 14 or 21 ms count once, as such a run takes one place in the probe order (session 20150717, data check). Windows are taken inclusive at 1 ms, as get_mean_resp.m indexes t:t+window, a standard choice. Saccade onset is sample tsaccade in MATLAB's 1-based indexing, as select_bases.m reads it (tsaccade(i) + times).
Rates are mean spike counts per ms over the window times 1000, SE across presentations (the criterion's measure).

outcomes.statement: In example test trials of three neurons the S- and F-models follow the recorded firing rate, with Delta LL per spike up to 1.12 bits/spk for the S-model and 0.81 for the F-model in the best trials, and 0.19 to 0.46 (S) and 0.05 to 0.41 (F) in median trials.
outcomes.source: Results, The time-varying encoding models accurately predict single trial spike response modulations across saccades, paragraph 1; Figure 3
outcomes.quote: The trials on the left show examples of high prediction accuracy (from top to bottom, Δ LL / spk = 1.12, 0.80, and 0.63 bits/spk for the S-model; and Δ LL / spk = 0.81, 0.47, and 0.55 bits/spk for the F-model)
outcomes.notes: Needs the S-model fitted per neuron (D4) and the F-model. The notebook ports the parameter selection of select_bases.m and times it on one neuron and probe: 290,628 stimulus-basis parameters and 58,125,600 single-parameter fits per neuron. The port took 2.2 to 6.7 ms per fit in the runs of this attempt, 345 to 1,040 hours on 4 CPUs for the selection step of the 41 neurons, far over the 60 minute notebook limit and the five hours of an author run. A fully batched port, not written here, would need at least 11.5 to 27.5 CPU hours (2.9 to 6.9 hours on 4 CPUs) for one selection per neuron, before the full S-model fit and the other models the claim needs. Not run beyond that benchmark; no model was fitted.

outcomes.statement: The N-model predicts perisaccadic spikes no better than fixation spikes (0.13 against 0.12 bits/spk, p = 0.26).
outcomes.source: Results, The time-varying encoding models accurately predict single trial spike response modulations across saccades, paragraph 3; Figure 5A
outcomes.quote: The N-model is no better at predicting the spike times during the perisaccadic period compared to the fixation period (Δ LL / spk = 0.12 ± 0.02 (mean ± SE) bits/spk during fixation vs. 0.13 ± 0.02 (mean ± SE) bits/spk during saccade, p-value = 0.26).
outcomes.notes: Needs the N-model, which the paper describes only as the model of ref [48] (Methods, Model evaluation, "as detailed in [48]") and the Results paragraph on Fig 4. The reference list is not in the text read, the code repository holds no N-model, and main_lists.mat has only its per-neuron classification (nsglm_list). The claims file (O8) blocks the claim when ref [48] cannot be identified. Fitting any such model for 41 neurons would also meet the cost of the S-model claims. After the round-2 verification, ref [48] was identified from the version of record's reference list as Akbarian et al. (2018), IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 65(2):241-253, doi:10.1109/TBME.2017.2762687 (open as PMC5796416). That paper describes the N-model (stimulus, gain, offset and post-spike kernels on raised-cosine bases, fitted by coordinate descent with cross-validated ridge and L1 penalties) but gives no code. This attempt did not implement it, so the claim stays blocked as verified; a later attempt can test it with the N-model taken from that paper, as O8 says.

outcomes.statement: The S-model predicts perisaccadic spikes better than fixation spikes (0.30 against 0.24 bits/spk, p < 0.001).
outcomes.source: Results, The time-varying encoding models accurately predict single trial spike response modulations across saccades, paragraph 3; Figure 5A
outcomes.quote: For the S-model, the prediction accuracy increases in the perisaccadic period (Δ LL / spk = 0.24 ± 0.02 (mean ± SE) bits/spk during fixation vs. 0.30 ± 0.02 (mean ± SE) bits/spk during saccade, p-value < 0.001).

outcomes.statement: The F-model also predicts perisaccadic spikes better than fixation spikes (0.18 against 0.14 bits/spk, p = 0.003).
outcomes.source: Results, The time-varying encoding models accurately predict single trial spike response modulations across saccades, paragraph 3; Figure 5A
outcomes.quote: The F-model, despite being based on an approximation of the S-model, also shows greater prediction accuracy during the perisaccadic period compared to fixation (Δ LL / spk = 0.14 ± 0.01 (mean ± SE) bits/spk during fixation vs. 0.18 ± 0.02 (mean ± SE) bits/spk during saccade, p-value = 0.003).

outcomes.source: Results, The time-varying encoding models accurately predict single trial spike response modulations across saccades, paragraph 3; Figure 5A
outcomes.quote: Both the S-, and F-models outperform the N-model during both the fixation (S-model vs. N-model: p-value < 0.001; F-model vs. N-model: p-value = 0.001) and perisaccadic (S-model vs. N-model: p-value < 0.001; F-model vs. N-model: p-value < 0.001) periods.
outcomes.notes: Needs the S-model fitted per neuron (D4), the F-model and the N-model (ref [48]). outcomes.notes: Converting grid positions to dva needs each session's grid position and probe spacing. The files hold only probe codes on the 9 x 9 grid, the data descriptor gives no geometry, the code repository has none (get_info.m gives only the 9 x 9 size), and the paper gives only the ranges of grid extent and spacing (Methods, paragraph 1).

findings.statement: The data set does not give the saccade direction of each session, each neuron's RF, FF and ST probe, the position and spacing of the probe grid in each session, or which of the two monkeys each session comes from. The probes are only in main_lists.mat of the paper's code repository, and the grid geometry is nowhere, so the RF centres of S1 Fig cannot be computed.

The paper and the descriptor say each probe lasted 7 ms with exactly one probe on screen at each time, and that "In each condition, a complete sequence of 81 probe stimuli was presented throughout the length of a trial." In the files 91.5% of probe runs last 7 ms, 5.6% last 6 ms, most others 14 or 21 ms and a few 8 to 28 ms, and the sequences contain gaps of 7 to 28 ms with no probe (code 0), nearly all of 10, 11, 20 or 21 ms. The probe order holds 75 codes in session 20150511 and 80 in 20150927 and 20150929. In every session but 20150717 the order restarts from its first probe 35 to 296 ms after saccade onset in most trials, so each probe is shown 2 to 4 times per trial. The arrays are 3000 ms long with probes until 1468 to 2371 ms, while the paper gives trials of 2100 to 2300 ms.

main_lists.mat in the code repository holds five 41 x 6 tables besides probe_list (nuron_list, nsglm_list, twobm_list, gauss_list, aggat_list) that no code reads and nothing documents. Their column sums match the paper's counts (nuron_list 8, 23, 23 and 37; aggat_list and nuron_list together 7, 18, 20 and 24, against the paper's 7, 20 and 24 for the A-model), so they appear to be the per-neuron classifications of Figures 1, 5 and 6.

The docx descriptor was not compared, which the verifier says bears on no conclusion.

paper_notes.statement: The Methods test each effect with a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test but do not say what is paired. Pairing by trial is impossible in these data, as no trial shows the same probe in both windows; pairing by condition gives 8 suppressed, 8 FF-remapping and 11 ST-remapping neurons against the paper's 8, 23 and 37. An unpaired test on every millisecond a probe is on gives 12, 17 and 31, and a signed-rank test over the 1 ms bins of the smoothed response curves gives 15, 19 and 34. Question for the authors: which presentations, pairs and test produced the classification of Figure 1 (and the nuron_list of main_lists.mat)? The example neurons' fixation rates also differ slightly from the paper's while their perisaccadic rates match (RF example 56.94 against 60.89 spk/s; FF, ST and both-effects examples 0.07 to 0.19 spk/s lower), and no single fixation window between -560 to -440 ms and -160 to -40 ms matches them all, so the fixation set used for Figure 1 is not the -500 to -100 ms the Methods give, or not only that.

The N-model of Figure 5 is described only by reference [48], Akbarian et al. (2018), IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 65(2):241-253, doi:10.1109/TBME.2017.2762687 (open as PMC5796416), and the code repository holds no code for it, nor for the Wilcoxon and McNemar tests, the partial F-models, the prevalence maps or the detectability analysis. Question for the authors: is there code for the N-model as fitted here?

entries.title: Perisaccadic responses of MT neurons (Niknam et al. 2019)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Niknam, Akbarian, Clark, Zamani, Noudoost and Nategh (2019) on CRCNS mt-3, which holds the spike trains, probe sequences and saccade times of 41 MT neurons from 11 sessions. It links the neurons to the RF, FF and ST probes listed in the paper's code, and tests the recorded saccadic suppression, FF- and ST-remapping of Figure 1. The model claims (S-, F-, A- and N-models, Figures 3 to 8) are blocked, with the cost of the S-model timed.
